examples.title: In a Form
Forwarded ref

accessibility:
- **One field:** the code is in one `<input>`, named by the label, so a screen reader announces a single text field with the code as its value. The boxes are drawn with `aria-hidden`, so nothing reads them a second time, or as a run of separate fields.
- **Say how long the code is in the label,** as in "Enter the 6-digit code", since the boxes that show it are hidden from a screen reader. The `message` isn't tied to the input, so a screen reader doesn't read it when the field takes focus. If the length lives in help text of your own, point the input's `aria-describedby` at it.
- **Masked,** the input is a password field, so a screen reader doesn't read the code out.
- **The keyboard a phone shows** is the number pad by default, through `inputMode="numeric"`, and the full keyboard with `type="alphanumeric"`.
- **Focus** shows on the boxes, since the input itself is transparent: the box at the caret, or every selected box, gets Bulma's focus ring, and an empty box at the caret draws a blinking caret. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the caret stays drawn and doesn't blink.
- **Forced colors:** in Windows high contrast mode the box at the caret is outlined in the system's highlight color, where Bulma's focus ring, a shadow, is gone, the caret is drawn in the system's text color, and a disabled box takes the system's color for disabled text.
summary: The `PinInput` component is a field for a short code, such as a one-time code or a PIN, drawn as a row of boxes with one character in each. The code lives in one real `<input>` that lies over the boxes, so it is one field to a screen reader, and paste, autofill from a text message and password managers work on it as they do on any input. The boxes draw what it holds, and the box at the caret, or every box in a selection, shows Bulma's focus look.

parts.summary: The `PinInput` component is a field for a short code, such as a one-time code or a PIN, drawn as a row of boxes with one character in each. The code lives in one real `<input>` that lies over the boxes, so it is one field to a screen reader, and paste, autofill from a text message and password managers work on it as they do on any input. The boxes draw what it holds, and the box at the caret, or every box in a selection, shows Bulma's focus look.

props.name: label
props.description: Field label. Automatically associated with the input that holds the code via `htmlFor`, so a screen reader announces one field under this name. Uses your `id` when provided, otherwise a generated one. Dropped inside an outer `Field`, whose own label associates instead when that `Field` generates a target id (not `grouped`/`hasAddons`, no explicit `labelProps.htmlFor`) and you set no `id` here.

props.name: labelProps
props.description: Props for the label element. An explicit `htmlFor` here overrides the automatic association (no id is generated then).

props.name: id
props.description: Applied to the input that holds the code (the labellable control), not the row of boxes.

props.name: length
props.description: How many characters the code has. Each gets a box, and it is the input's `maxLength`.

props.name: value
props.description: The code (controlled). Only its first `length` characters are shown and submitted.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The code to start with (uncontrolled). Only its first `length` characters are kept.

props.name: type
props.description: What the code takes. A digit from any script, such as an Arabic-Indic or a Persian one, goes in as its ASCII digit, so the code reaches `onChange`, `onComplete` and the form as `0` to `9`. Anything else typed or pasted is dropped, and the caret stays where it was. The input stays a text field either way, so a code keeps its leading zeros.

props.name: isMasked
props.description: Shows a dot in each filled box in place of its character, and makes the input a password field, so a screen reader doesn't read the code out either.

props.name: color
props.description: Bulma color for the boxes, the colors an `Input` takes.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the code each time it changes. A paste replaces the whole code with what was pasted, kept to what `type` takes and cut to `length`, and a paste with nothing the code takes changes nothing.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Called with the code when a change makes it `length` characters long, such as typing the last character, a paste or autofill. It fires once for each change that fills the last box with a new code, and never on a render. A `value` you set yourself doesn't call it.

props.name: labelSize
props.description: Size for the label (used in horizontal layouts).

props.name: fieldClassName
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the Field wrapper.

extraProps.name: name
extraProps.description: Form field name, on the input, so a form submits the code under it.

extraProps.name: autoComplete
extraProps.description: Lets the browser offer a code it received by text message, and tells a password manager this is a one-time code.

extraProps.name: inputMode
extraProps.description: The keyboard a phone shows: `"numeric"` with `type="number"`, `"text"` with `type="alphanumeric"`.

extraProps.name: pattern
extraProps.description: Exactly `length` of what `type` takes, `[0-9]{6}` by default, so a form with `required` won't submit a partial code. Any non-empty partial code fails it, `required` or not.

extraProps.name: className
extraProps.description: Additional CSS classes for the row of boxes.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the input that holds the code.

parts.catchAll: All standard <input> attributes and Bulma helper props
parts.helperPropsNote: Helper props go on the `.pin-input` `<div>`, the row of boxes, with `className`. The other attributes go on the `<input>` that holds the code.
